result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the illusion of separation—the belief that we are fundamentally divided from one another, from nature, and from the deeper currents of life. I would replace it with an unshakable recognition that everything is interconnected, that every act of harm or kindness ripples outward in ways we can’t always see, and that true power lies in understanding our shared existence.

This wouldn’t erase conflict or difference, but it would shift the foundation of how we relate to one another. Instead of scarcity and fear driving our choices, we’d act from a place of abundance and mutual care. Systems built on exploitation would crumble because they couldn’t survive in a world where people see themselves in the eyes of others. Nature wouldn’t be a resource to extract but a living web to which we belong.

It’s not a simple fix—it’s a revolution of perception. But if enough people saw the world this way, the structures of oppression, greed, and violence would have no choice but to transform. The world wouldn’t be perfect, but it would finally have a chance to heal.
